'''''Echinopsis spachiana''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]] including '''''Soehrensia spachiana''''' and '''''Trichocereus spachianus''''', commonly known as the '''golden torch''', '''(white) torch cactus''' or '''golden column''', is a species of [[cactus]] native to [[South America]]. It is commonly cultivated as a pot or rockery plant worldwide. It has a columnar [[Habit (biology)|habit]], with a lime-green cylindrical body with {{cvt|1–2|cm|in|1}} long golden spines.

==Description==
''Echinopsis spachiana'' grows as a cactus with a columnar habit, reaching 2 m (7 ft) high, with a diameter of {{convert|5–6|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=4}}.<ref name=Ande01/> Vertical branches arise from the base of the plant.<ref name=britton>{{cite book |year=1919 | volume=1| title=The Cactaceae : descriptions and illustrations of plants of the cactus family |author1=Britton, Nathaniel Lord |author2=Rose, Joseph Nelson |location=Washington, D.C. |publisher=Carnegie Institution of Washington | pages=130–32 | url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/32089041 }}</ref> Each column has 10–15 rounded ribs. The large [[areole]]s are around 1 cm apart, and have wavy yellow hairs. The straight spines are red-yellow initially, fading to white as they age. The central spine is around {{convert|1–2|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=4}} long, and is surrounded by 8 to 10 smaller radial spines that are {{convert|0.4–1|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=4}} in length. The white flowers are 15 cm (6 in) across and {{convert|18–20|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=4}} long,<ref name=Ande01>{{Cite book |last=Anderson |first=Edward F. |date=2001 |title=The Cactus Family |publication-place=Pentland, Oregon |publisher=Timber Press |isbn=978-0-88192-498-5 |page=280}}</ref> part of which is an 8 cm long tube. In the northern hemisphere, the flowers appear in June–July and open at night.<ref name=riccobono/>

==Taxonomy==
French botanist [[Charles Antoine Lemaire]] described the species as ''Cereus spachianus'' in 1839, in honour of his countryman [[Édouard Spach]]. The type specimen was collected in Argentina, though where in the country is unclear.<ref name=britton/> [[Alwin Berger]] erected the subgenus ''Trichocereus'' in 1905, incorporating this species.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Berger, Alwin | year=1905 | title=A systematic revision of the genus ''Cereus'' Mill. | pages = 57–86 [73] | url=http://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=hvd.32044107241036;view=1up;seq=21 | journal=Missouri Botanical Garden Annual Report 1905| volume=1905 | doi=10.2307/2400072 | jstor=2400072 | hdl=2027/hvd.32044107241036 | hdl-access=free | url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[Vincenzo Riccobono]] elevated ''Trichocereus'' to genus status in 1909,<ref name=riccobono>{{cite journal | author=Riccobono, Vincenzo |title=Sp. 1° Trichocereus Spachianus (Berg. l. c. p. 73).  | year=1909 | page=237 | url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/40173026 | journal=Bollettino del R. Orto Botanico di Palermo | volume=8}}</ref> and hence it was for many years known as ''Trichocereus spachianus''. The genus encompassed a number of columnar cacti, before being subsumed into ''[[Echinopsis]]''. A 2012 genetic analysis of [[chloroplast]] DNA indicates ''Echinopsis'' is made up of several divergent lineages. ''E. spachiana'' was not included in the study but is thought to be related to a ''Helianthocereus'' clade.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Schlumpberger, Boris O. |author2=Renner, Susanne S. |title=Molecular phylogenetics of ''Echinopsis'' (Cactaceae): Polyphyly at all levels and convergent evolution of pollination modes and growth forms|journal= American Journal of Botany |year=2012 | volume=99 |issue= 8|pages=1335–49 | doi=10.3732/ajb.1100288 | pmid=22859654|doi-access=free }}</ref> {{As of|2026|February}}, [[Plants of the World Online]] placed it in the genus ''[[Echinopsis]]''.<ref name=POWO_88507-2/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Echinopsis spachiana'' is native to northwestern Argentina around Icaño and Santiago del Estero province and Bolivia.<ref name=britton/> It has been introduced elsewhere, including Mexico, the Canary Islands, and Spain,<ref name=POWO_88507-2/> and is a declared weed in South Africa.<ref>{{cite report |year=2003 |author1=Neville, Geoffrey |author2=Howard, W. |author3=Murphy, Sean J. |author4=Preston, Guy |title=Invasive Alien Species in Southern Africa: a: national reports & directory of resources |publisher=Global Invasive Species Programme |location=Cape Town, South Africa |url=http://www.capetown.gov.za/en/EnvironmentalResourceManagement/publications/Documents/IAS_in_Southern_Africa-National_Reports+Directory_of_Resources.pdf |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303185535/http://www.capetown.gov.za/en/EnvironmentalResourceManagement/publications/Documents/IAS_in_Southern_Africa-National_Reports+Directory_of_Resources.pdf |archivedate=2016-03-03 }}</ref><ref name="c877">{{cite web | title=Echinopsis spachiana (Lemaire) H.
